extracted.intended_audience: journalists, Apple developers, historians, and general readers researching Apple media events
extracted.subtask_description: A chronological, wiki-style listing of Apple special events and WWDC keynotes that records dates, venues, taglines, products/software announced, streaming details, and other recurring attributes of Apple's media events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event tagline
rubrics_metrics.description: Apple events are commonly promoted with a short tagline used on invitations (examples: "See you on the 7th", "Let us loop you in", "Time flies.", "Hi, Speed", "California streaming", "Unleashed", "Peek performance", "Far out.").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taglines appear in event invitations and are frequently referenced in summaries. They often hint at the theme or focus of the event and are a standard metadata element when documenting or reporting an Apple event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue and date (location/time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each event entry records the date and physical venue (e.g., Steve Jobs Theater, Apple Park, Moscone West, Bill Graham Civic Auditorium, Brooklyn Academy of Music) and often the local start time (e.g., 10 a.m. PDT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation should include precise venue and date information; notes in the page also distinguish in-person, virtual, or hybrid formats. Time zone is commonly given (Pacific Time/PDT).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience invited (press, media, developers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The page repeatedly notes who was invited for each event (press media, developers, or both), e.g., "Apple invited the press media and developers" or "Apple invited the press media for its event".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different event types target different audiences (WWDC for developers, special events for press/media). Recording the invited audience helps clarify the event's intended focus and coverage expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcements and product/software reveals
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries list the primary announcements (hardware and software) made at each event, e.g., new iPhone models, iPad Pro, watchOS, iOS, macOS, new chips (M1, M2, M3), Apple TV updates, Apple services (Apple TV+, Apple Arcade), and OS release names and dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When documenting or writing about an event, include the specific products/services revealed and any immediately announced release dates or shipping/preorder information. The page often notes which OS releases followed the keynote and how many days later they became available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Livestream and platform availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The page records whether the keynote was streamed live and on which platforms (Apple's website, Apple TV channel, YouTube—first time in 2019, and compatibility notes such as Windows users able to watch via Microsoft Edge in 2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include streaming availability and platform changes (e.g., first-time YouTube stream, availability on specific browsers). Note whether the keynote was live or pre-recorded (especially during COVID-19 when keynotes were pre-recorded).

rubrics_metrics.name: Event format and production (in-person, virtual, pre-recorded, hybrid)
rubrics_metrics.description: The page differentiates event formats: in-person events at venues, fully virtual events (WWDC 2020 pre-recorded), and hybrid approaches (online with in-person experiences at Apple Park).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record whether the event was live/in-person, virtual/pre-recorded, or hybrid. The COVID-19 pandemic prompted a shift to pre-recorded virtual keynotes and later limited in-person experiences, which is important context for coverage and archival records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting entertainment (performances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many Apple events include musical performances by named artists (examples: OneRepublic, Sia, Panic! at the Disco, Lana Del Rey, Weezer, Walk the Moon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing events, note any on-stage performances or entertainers, as these are recurring elements of Apple's presentation style and can be noteworthy in press coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release timing and follow-up (OS/software release dates)
rubrics_metrics.description: The page frequently notes the timing between an event and subsequent software releases (e.g., "iOS 12, watchOS 5 and tvOS 12 were released five days later", "iOS 13 and watchOS 6 were released nine days later").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any announced or later actual release dates for software/hardware and the interval from announcement to release; this detail is commonly tracked in event summaries and press coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wikipedia citation/reliability notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections are sometimes flagged with: "This section does not cite any sources. Please help improve this section by adding citations to reliable sources. Unsourced material may be challenged and removed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a wiki page maintenance guideline, uncited assertions should be supported by reliable sources. When using content from this page for reporting or scholarship, verify facts against cited primary sources because unsourced material may be unreliable.
